events.title: Balboa Sights the Pacific
events.description: Spanish conquistador Vasco Núñez de Balboa climbed a peak in present-day Panama. He became the first European known to have seen the Pacific Ocean from the New World, which he named the South Sea.
events.significance: The sighting opened the way for Spanish exploration and expansion along the Pacific coast of the Americas.

events.title: Peace of Augsburg Signed
events.description: Holy Roman Emperor Charles V and the forces of the Protestant Schmalkaldic League signed the Peace of Augsburg. It ended a bitter religious struggle within the Holy Roman Empire.
events.significance: The treaty permanently recognized the religious division of Christendom within the Empire, allowing rulers to choose between Lutheranism and Catholicism.

events.title: Congress Sends the Bill of Rights to the States
events.description: The first U.S. Congress approved twelve proposed constitutional amendments and sent them to the states for ratification.
events.significance: Ten of them were ratified in 1791 as the Bill of Rights, which guarantees core freedoms such as speech, religion and fair trial.

events.title: Little Rock Nine Enter Central High School
events.description: Nine Black students entered Little Rock Central High School in Arkansas under protection from federal troops. President Eisenhower had sent the troops after state officials and angry crowds blocked integration.
events.significance: The episode became a landmark test of federal authority to enforce school desegregation and a defining moment of the civil rights movement.
